title: Rupee appreciates for third consecutive day as oil dips - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The rupee appreciated for the third consecutive day, opening at ₹93.30 per US dollar as crude oil prices continued to fall and market sentiment improved.

The local currency rose 18 paise at open on November 18, marking its third consecutive session of gains. It was trading at around ₹93.40 a dollar during the first few hours of the session. Rupee has appreciated by over 90 paise in the last three sessions. It last saw these levels on April 17, 2026, when it was at ₹92.60.

Crude oil prices fall as US inventory build outweighs West Asia tensions

The increase is attributed to lower crude prices and renewed FPI interest in Indian stocks.

Anil Bhansali, Head of Treasury at Finrex Treasury Advisors, said, “This notable appreciation-pushing the rupee to fresh multi-month highs-was primarily fueled by a steep overnight drop in Brent crude oil prices toward the $91.50 mark, which eases India’s import bill and inflation concerns, alongside sustained foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows. Together, lower energy costs and steady dollar selling by foreign and custodian banks comfortably outweighed broader strength in the U.S. Dollar Index.”

Flat opening as Nvidia earnings beat softens Wall Street’s blow; Bank Nifty holds near record high

Cooling oil prices also helped, with with Brent crude futures trading at around $92.5 a barrel.

On the currency’s further movements, Bhansali said exporters remain uncovered, while importers have good opportunities to hedge in the near term. “Exporters need to wait for an upside before they sell $ while importers may continue buying the dips for their near term and cash imports,” he noted.

Analysts say that, under current conditions, the rupee-dollar pair could go as high as ₹91.50 in the near term.
